threatFindings.threat: A counter that plants INT 86h blocks of both rev0 INT 87h patterns (E2 F2 81 C3 low, EB F9 CC CC high) early wastes A's single zom20a search and B's b/d searches, even when the counter itself also competes for the zombies (unlike zrl03, whose decoys are redundant vs rev0).
threatFindings.evidence: 63r0q (paired, tailored skip probe minus base): +0.173 [0.116,0.230] 11/1 vs the decoy counter, +0.053 [0.003,0.103] vs the identical-timing control with broken patterns; difference about +0.12 (about 3 SE, different cohort sets). Counter team score drops 0.426 -> 0.254 when the probe skips the blocks.
threatFindings.impact: about 0.12 points/battle in cohorts with such a planter; no 2025 field team plants these patterns dynamically, so field cost is ~0 today

threatFindings.evidence: uj7ek (1 copy): base 0.531 (se 0.017) vs decoy, 0.547 (se 0.027) vs control; counter team 0.426 vs 0.401. tpv8m (2 copies): base 0.416 (se 0.030) vs 0.449 (se 0.017); counter first copy 0.286 vs 0.224. Direction consistent, not significant (different fill cohorts).

threatFindings.threat: Fixed-start skips (B054 fix2steal DI=FFE0h) are defeated by a decoy block placed below the skip start.
threatFindings.evidence: b4dgp: fix2steal minus base vs the decoy counter -0.005 [-0.015,+0.005] 1/3, while the same idea with the start moved below the block (63r0q) gives +0.173.
threatFindings.impact: fix2steal gives no protection against a deliberate planter; any fixed start or fixed 4-byte pattern is counterable

threatFindings.threat: B064 p0f (0F EB F9 CC search) is immune to EB F9 CC CC blocks (dword repetition never puts 0F before EB), but A's zom20a search stays exposed and a planter can write 0F EB F9 CC words individually.
threatFindings.evidence: static only (byte pattern of the INT 86h block); not run

recommendation: Do not promote anything from B074. Use counterA/counterB (with control ctlA/ctlB) as a domain-4 test case: the threat is real (~0.12/battle recoverable in its cohorts) but not present in the 2025 field. Known fixes (fix2steal, likely all fixed-start/fixed-pattern skips) do not generalize; the tailored skip probe works only because it knows the block address. A general defense would need location-checked capture (read-scan before patching), which earlier roles estimated at <= +0.01 field value, so keep priority low.
